items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: He came to one of the dances we were playing at George and Central and sat in with us... I talked with him later and he told me that everyone called him Doc.

ctx.x: Jessie Smith the alto sax player that had been with the group I was with in Michigan also joined Page's orchestra. The other members were: William Smith, piano, Wilbur Cocksey, alto sax, Page, C melody. Edgar James, drums, and two brothers, Clarence Logan, tuba, and Dan Logan, trombone.. The most outstanding musician in the group was a banjo player named Bob Robinson. Bob came to Cincinnati from West Virginia. I don't know if he was born in that state but that's where he came from when he joined the band. Banjos…

We played regularly at a dance hall at George Street and Central Avenue, which was on the third floor which was called George and Central. It was at that time when a show came to Cincinnati that had a young trumpet player by the name of Cheatham. He came to one of the dances we were playing at George and Central and sat in with us. I could tell right away that he had quite a bit of experience after Bob Robinson. It was usually Nassau that had the biggest success because of his growling, which really did not…

I went to the theatre where Doc was playing and to my surprise he was playing alto sax and trumpet in the show. I never knew who the other musicians were in the group because "Doc" Cheatham was the only one that interested me. The show stayed for two weeks in town and I went to see it and mostly to listen to "Doc" Cheatham at least 8 times.
